hello.note: Polite, and also used as goodbye. To a friend or child: γεια σου (yia sou).

goodbye.note: Γεια σας (yia sas) is just as common. Leaving a shop: καλή συνέχεια (kalí sinéchia).

please.note: Also the reply to 'thank you', and what you say when answering the phone.

thank_you.note: Thank you very much: ευχαριστώ πολύ (efcharistó polí).

youre_welcome.note: Literally 'nothing'. Παρακαλώ (parakaló), the word for please, is just as common.

yes.note: Sounds like 'neh' — don't mistake it for no! More formal: μάλιστα (málista).

no.note: Before ι or ε, χ is a soft hiss like the h in 'huge' (German 'ich'), not the 'loch' sound.

sorry.note: Also used to get someone's attention or to squeeze past.

excuse_me.note: A quick συγγνώμη (signómi) works too and is very common.

good_morning.note: Used until about midday; after that, καλησπέρα (kalispéra).

how_are_you.note: Greek uses ; as its question mark. To a friend: τι κάνεις; (ti kánis).

whats_your_name.note: To a friend: πώς σε λένε; (pos se léne). More formal: πώς λέγεστε; (pos léyeste).

nice_to_meet_you.note: Also: χάρηκα (chárika). The usual reply is επίσης (epísis), 'likewise'.

where_from.note: To a friend: από πού είσαι; (apó pou íse).

im_from.note: Countries take 'the': είμαι από την Αγγλία (íme apó tin Anglía).

speak_slowly.text: Μπορείτε να μιλάτε πιο αργά, παρακαλώ;
speak_slowly.roman: Boríte na miláte pio argá, parakaló?

where.note: Keep the accent: που without it means 'that' or 'which'.

what.note: To ask someone to repeat, the polite way is ορίστε; (oríste) or πώς; (pos).

who.note: When asking about a woman: ποια; (pia).

one.note: Before a masculine noun: ένας (énas); before a feminine one: μία (mía).

two.note: The δ is soft, like 'th' in 'this'.

three.note: Before masculine and feminine nouns: τρεις (tris).

four.note: Before masculine and feminine nouns: τέσσερις (tésseris).

seven.note: Also επτά (eptá), the formal form you will see in writing.

eight.note: Also οκτώ (októ), the formal form you will see in writing.

nine.note: Sounds like 'e-NYA'. Also εννέα (ennéa), the formal form you will see in writing.

coffee.note: Greek coffee: ελληνικός (ellinikós). Iced: φρέντο (fréndo) or φραπέ (frapé).

tea.note: Two syllables, stress on the first: TSA-ee.

bread.note: Pronounce the p: ps as in 'lapse'.

menu_please.note: Το μενού (to menoú) is also used.

train_station.note: Locals often just say ο σταθμός (o stathmós), 'the station'.

want_to_go.note: Put στο/στη(ν)/στον before the place: θέλω να πάω στην Αθήνα (stin Athína).

too_expensive.note: ακριβό agrees with the item: ακριβός (akrivós) if masculine, ακριβή (akriví) if feminine.

id_like_this.note: Also: θα πάρω αυτό (tha páro aftó), 'I'll take this'.

just_looking.note: Add ευχαριστώ (efcharistó). Also: ρίχνω μια ματιά (ríchno mia matiá).

open.note: Signs often use capitals and the formal spelling: ΑΝΟΙΚΤΟ.

big.note: Neuter form; masculine μεγάλος (megálos), feminine μεγάλη (megáli).

small.note: Neuter form; masculine μικρός (mikrós), feminine μικρή (mikrí).

good_evening.note: A greeting from the afternoon on. Leaving in the evening: καλό βράδυ (kaló vrádi).

see_you_later.note: Literally 'we say them', i.e. we'll talk. For later today: τα λέμε αργότερα (ta léme argótera).

wait_moment.note: Literally 'one minute'. Also: περιμένετε λίγο (periménete lígo).

dont_feel_well.note: Also: δεν αισθάνομαι καλά (den esthánome kalá).

allergic.note: A woman says: είμαι αλλεργική σε … (íme alleryikí se …). σε + 'the' → στο/στη(ν)/στα.

be_careful.note: A warning shout. To one person: πρόσεχε! (próseche); polite or plural: προσέξτε! (proséxte).

i_like_it.note: For more than one thing: μου αρέσουν (mou arésoun).

im_tired.note: A woman says: είμαι κουρασμένη (íme kourasméni).

im_happy.note: A woman says: είμαι χαρούμενη (íme charoúmeni).

welcome.note: To one friend: καλώς ήρθες! (kalós írthes). The guest replies: καλώς σας βρήκα (kalós sas vríka).

congratulations.note: For a job well done: μπράβο! (brávo).

my_family.note: οικογένεια gains a second accent before μου; the stress falls on -niá.

father.note: Everyday: μπαμπάς (bambás). Both parents: οι γονείς (i gonís).

brother.note: Also αδελφός (adelfós), the more formal form you will see in writing.

sister.note: Also αδελφή (adelfí), the more formal form you will see in writing.

child.note: Son: γιος (yios); daughter: κόρη (kóri). Children: παιδιά (pediá).

this_is_my_friend.note: For a female friend: αυτή είναι η φίλη μου (aftí íne i fíli mou).

are_you_married.note: To a woman: είστε παντρεμένη; (íste pandreméni).

have_children.note: To a friend: έχεις παιδιά; (échis pediá).

monday.note: Literally 'second': Greeks count from Sunday. On Monday: τη Δευτέρα (ti Deftéra).

tuesday.note: Literally 'third'. In Greece the unlucky day is Tuesday the 13th, not Friday.

friday.note: Not a number like the others: it means 'preparation' (for the Sabbath).

saturday.note: From 'Sabbath'. The double ββ sounds like a single v.

weekend.note: Saturday + Sunday in one word. Have a good one: καλό Σαββατοκύριακο! (kaló Savvatokíriako).

what_day.note: Also: τι μέρα έχουμε σήμερα; (ti méra échoume símera).

next_week.note: More casually: την άλλη εβδομάδα (tin álli evdomáda).

fifteen.note: From 13 on it is ten + unit: δεκατρία (dekatría) 13, δεκαέξι (dekaéxi) 16.

twenty.note: Just add the unit: είκοσι ένα (íkosi éna), 21.

hundred.note: Before another number it becomes εκατόν: εκατόν είκοσι (ekatón íkosi), 120.

how_old.note: To a friend or child: πόσων χρονών είσαι; (póson chronón íse).

years_old.note: E.g. είμαι τριάντα χρονών (íme triánda chronón). Χρονών is often dropped.

red.note: Neuter form; masculine κόκκινος (kókkinos), feminine κόκκινη (kókkini).

blue.note: Never changes form. Light or sky blue: γαλάζιο (galázio).

green.note: Neuter form; masculine πράσινος (prásinos), feminine πράσινη (prásini).

yellow.note: Neuter form; masculine κίτρινος (kítrinos), feminine κίτρινη (kítrini).

black.note: Neuter form; masculine μαύρος (mávros), feminine μαύρη (mávri).

white.note: Neuter form; masculine άσπρος (áspros), feminine άσπρη (áspri). Formal: λευκό (lefkó).

this_one.note: Neuter form. For a masculine noun: αυτόν εδώ (aftón edó); feminine: αυτή εδώ (aftí edó).

that_one.note: Neuter form. In everyday speech also αυτό εκεί (aftó ekí).

another_one.note: For a masculine item: άλλον έναν (állon énan); feminine: άλλη μία (álli mía).

its_hot.note: For the weather only. 'I feel hot' is ζεσταίνομαι (zesténome).

its_cold.note: For the weather only. 'I feel cold' is κρυώνω (krióno).

its_windy.note: Literally 'it blows'. Also: έχει αέρα (échi aéra).

beautiful_day.note: Also: είναι πανέμορφη μέρα (íne panémorfi méra).

summer.note: Before the holidays people wish each other καλό καλοκαίρι! (kaló kalokéri).

have_reservation.note: Add your name: στο όνομα … (sto ónoma …).

wifi_password.text: Ποιος είναι ο κωδικός του Wi-Fi;
wifi_password.roman: Pios íne o kodikós tou Wi-Fi?
wifi_password.note: Wi-Fi is written and said as in English. κωδικός (kodikós) is the usual word for a password.

check_out_time.text: Μέχρι τι ώρα πρέπει να αφήσω το δωμάτιο;
check_out_time.roman: Méchri ti óra prépi na afíso to domátio?

map.note: Asking for one: έναν χάρτη, παρακαλώ (énan chárti, parakaló).

is_this_seat_free.note: Or: είναι πιασμένη; (íne piasméni), 'is it taken?'

what_do_you_do.note: To a friend: τι δουλειά κάνεις; (ti douliá kánis).

i_work_in.note: E.g. σε τράπεζα (se trápeza), at a bank. σε + 'the' → στο/στη(ν)/στις: στις πωλήσεις (stis polísis), in sales.

im_student.note: A woman says: είμαι φοιτήτρια (íme fitítria). A school pupil is μαθητής (mathitís).

meeting.note: For an internal work meeting, σύσκεψη (sískepsi) is also common.

im_busy.note: A woman says: είμαι απασχολημένη (íme apascholiméni). Casually: έχω δουλειά (écho douliá).

day_off.note: I'm off today: έχω ρεπό σήμερα (écho repó símera).

colleague.note: Same word for a woman, with η: η συνάδελφος (i sinádelfos).

good_job.note: Μπράβο! (brávo) alone is the most common praise. To a friend: μπράβο σου! (brávo sou).

table_for_two.note: Often: για δύο άτομα (yia dío átoma), 'for two people'.

what_recommend.note: Also: τι είναι καλό σήμερα; (ti íne kaló símera), 'what's good today?'

vegetarian_food.note: Asking: έχετε κάτι χορτοφαγικό; (échete káti chortofayikó).

more_water.note: Another bottle: άλλο ένα νερό (állo éna neró).

no_sugar.note: Greek coffee with no sugar is σκέτος (skétos); medium sweet, μέτριος (métrios).

im_full.note: Also: είμαι χορτάτος (íme chortátos); a woman says χορτάτη (chortáti).

takeaway.note: In cafés also: για έξω (yia éxo). For here: για εδώ (yia edó).

it_was_delicious.note: About the whole meal: ήταν όλα πολύ νόστιμα (ítan óla polí nóstima).

head_hurts.note: Also: έχω πονοκέφαλο (écho ponokéfalo), 'I have a headache'.

medicine.note: Plural: φάρμακα (fármaka). Sold at the φαρμακείο (farmakío).

call_ambulance.note: People also say: πάρτε το ΕΚΑΒ! (párte to ékav), the ambulance service. Number: 166.

get_well.note: Literally 'may it pass'. Said to anyone who is ill or hurt.

lets_meet.note: Often as an invitation: πάμε για καφέ; (páme yia kafé), 'shall we go for a coffee?'

are_you_free.note: To a woman: είστε ελεύθερη αύριο; (íste eléftheri ávrio). Also: έχετε χρόνο αύριο; (échete chróno ávrio).

call_me.note: To a friend: πάρε με (páre me). Also: τηλεφωνήστε μου (tilefoníste mou).

your_number.note: To a friend: ποιο είναι το τηλέφωνό σου; (pio íne to tiléfonó sou).

have_nice_day.note: To a friend: καλή σου μέρα! (kalí sou méra). Also very common: καλή συνέχεια! (kalí sinéchia).

good_luck.note: Before an exam or a new job: καλή επιτυχία! (kalí epitichía).

happy_birthday.note: Literally 'many years'. Also said on name days and holidays.

thanks_a_lot.note: More polite: σας ευχαριστώ πολύ (sas efcharistó polí). Warmer still: πάρα πολύ (pára polí).

miss_you.note: Literally 'you are missing to me'. To several people: μου λείπετε (mou lípete).
